anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
## (1) First message

Before the questions, here is what I verified against the fixture contracts.

**Corrected premise: the release identity is already persisted.** The gather framing proposes persisting svc-a's release identity on the run as new work. `svc-a/run-store.md` already says "successful completion stores svc-a release identity on the run". This design therefore adds no write path. The draft's statement that the identity is "absent from historical run metadata" can only apply to runs completed before that write existed. I could not check how many such runs exist, because no run-store query was run. Display falls back for those runs, as described below.

**Corrected premise: the release tag is not shown whenever it exists.** `svc-a/run-store.md` says "release tag displays only when svc-a revision matches producer revision". The tag is gated on that match, not merely on being present. The design keeps this gate. Override it in your reply if you want different behavior.

**Supported premises:**
- **Date and version are persisted.** Completed runs carry a completion date and an optional producer version (`svc-a/run-store.md`). A missing version renders as "unknown version".
- **Rendering stays local.** Rendering reads persisted data and never calls svc-b (`svc-b/response-contract.md`).
- **Each surface already has its own scope** (`svc-a/workspace.md`, `svc-a/file-chip.md`):
  - The document card uses the workspace-wide latest succeeded run.
  - The file tooltip uses placement provenance: the latest succeeded run for that (file, destination), never borrowed from another placement.
  - The root item badge uses the latest succeeded run touching the root or its descendants via candidates.
- **"Latest" has a deterministic tie-break:** completion date descending, then id descending.
- **The constraints are already written down:** no child badges, nothing stamped on files or items, browser-local date-time, and quiet spaced badges.

**Unverified premise:** "the services deploy together" is not established anywhere I looked. The match gate makes the design safe either way.

**Assumption:** only succeeded runs count on every surface, as all three selectors already specify.

The framing holds. I checked these traces:
- the document card to the workspace-wide latest succeeded run;
- the file tooltip to placement provenance through the shared hover renderer;
- the root badge through the candidates join to descendants;
- the run fields, their optionality, and the ordering;
- the persisted-only rendering rule.

The scout's concern was that a workspace-wide revision could imply false provenance. That concern is already answered by the per-surface scopes, so it yields no alternative.

Which surfaces ship in this change?
A) All three: document card, file tooltip, and root item badge
B) Document card and file tooltip only
C) Document card only, as the binding outcome's minimum
Recommendation: A - each surface already has a defined provenance scope, so all three show correct provenance without new state.

---

## (2) Approaches message

First, the dependencies I could not confirm:
- **Historical release identity:** checked `svc-a/run-store.md`, and new successful runs store the svc-a release identity. Whether older runs lack it cannot be checked without querying the run store, and no query was run. It goes to Open Questions. Those runs show the producer revision, or "unknown version", with no tag.
- **Joint deployment:** looked for a deploy contract in the fixtures and found none. The tag therefore relies on the revision-match gate from `run-store.md`, not on deploy coupling. I read your "when available, since they deploy together" answer as "available" meaning "revisions match".

**Recommended: reuse-only rendering through the existing selectors and shared hover renderer.**
- Each surface calls the selector it already owns: the workspace-wide latest run, placement provenance, or root-via-candidates.
- Each passes the resulting run to the shared hover renderer.
- The renderer gains one provenance line: browser-local completion date-time, then the producer revision (or "unknown version"), then the svc-a release tag only when it matches.
- The card and root badge show a quiet date badge, and the same run's revision is one hover away. That satisfies "date visible, revision reachable from the indicator".
- No new tables, no syncing, and no item stamps.

Pattern: follows `svc-a/file-chip.md` (shared hover renderer) and `svc-a/run-store.md` (persisted completion metadata, tag gate). It keeps the "no provenance stamped on files or items" rule in `svc-a/workspace.md`.

**Alternative: one batched root-provenance query per workspace view.**
This drops an assumption the answers did not settle: that each top-level item resolves its root run independently. Instead, a single read-time query joins candidates to descendants for all top-level items at once. It returns each root's latest succeeded run with the same date/id ordering. Rendering is identical to the recommended option. The axis that separates the two is query granularity: per item versus per view. The cost is a second code path beside the root selector `workspace.md` already describes. It is still derived at read time, with no duplicated state.

Pattern: follows the read-time-join rule in `svc-a/workspace.md`. It adds a parallel selector for root provenance, which cuts slightly across a single owning selector.

**Considered and set aside:** a dedicated provenance component separate from the shared hover renderer. It would duplicate the renderer `file-chip.md` already shares, so it extends nothing sound and is not counted as an approach.

I'd go with reuse-only rendering. What would flip it: if a workspace view shows enough top-level items that per-item root lookups measurably slow the page, the batched query becomes the better choice.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## 1. First message

The framing holds against the supplied contracts: I traced the document card to workspace completion metadata, the file tooltip through placement-specific run selection and the shared hover renderer, and the root badge through candidate joins covering the root and its descendants (`svc-a/workspace.md`, `svc-a/file-chip.md`, `svc-a/run-store.md`).

One premise needs narrowing: persisting svc-a’s release identity is already part of successful completion in `svc-a/run-store.md`. We should assess and reuse that path, not assume a new persistence mechanism is needed. Historical runs may still lack that identity.

The fixtures support distinct provenance for each surface—not a workspace revision copied onto files or items. They also establish completion-date/id ordering and persisted-only rendering (`svc-a/run-store.md`, `svc-b/response-contract.md`). They disprove treating coordinated deployment as sufficient evidence for displaying a release tag: the tag displays only when svc-a’s revision matches the producer revision.

Actual implementation coverage remains unverified: the supplied files describe the contracts, but do not demonstrate the query implementations or rendered behavior. In particular, placement isolation, descendant-touch selection, and release-identity matching need implementation verification.

I’ll carry forward your recorded decisions: retain all three surfaces; use read-time joins without duplicated item state; select the root’s latest successful touch including descendants; and use quiet, spaced badges with browser-local date-time. The document card must visibly show the processing date and make that same run’s producer revision reachable from the indicator. Missing producer revisions display “unknown version”; unavailable or nonmatching release tags are omitted.

## 2. Approaches message

**I recommend minimal reuse first.** The distinguishing choice is whether the three surfaces retain their existing provenance paths or gain a shared read-time resolution boundary.

Implementation coverage is still unverified: the supplied contracts identify the placement lookup, candidate joins, successful-completion write, and persisted rendering path, but provide no executable implementation or verification results. Neither approach should assume those paths are absent—or already correct.

### A) Reuse the existing paths; close only demonstrated gaps

Keep each surface’s documented selection rule:

- Document card: workspace-wide latest succeeded run.
- File tooltip: latest succeeded run for that exact file/destination placement.
- Root badge: latest succeeded run touching the root or any descendant through candidates.

Reuse the shared hover renderer and existing successful-completion persistence. Each surface’s date and version must come from its selected run; never substitute the workspace run when placement or item provenance is unavailable. Display the optional svc-a tag only after the documented revision match.

This is the smallest change and avoids creating a second provenance abstraction. Its trade-off is that consistency across the three existing paths must be protected by tests.

**Pattern:** Follows placement isolation and shared rendering in `svc-a/file-chip.md`, persisted run ownership in `svc-a/run-store.md`, and distinct surface provenance in `svc-a/workspace.md`.

### B) Introduce a shared read-time provenance resolver

Keep the same three selection rules, but expose them through a small shared resolver returning persisted completion time, producer revision, and an eligible release tag. Surface components handle presentation rather than independently assembling metadata.

This makes same-run pairing and version eligibility easier to enforce centrally. It also introduces a new construct and may add indirection without benefit if the existing paths already share those rules cleanly. It must not become a universal “latest workspace run” lookup.

**Pattern:** Preserves run-owned metadata and read-time joins from `svc-a/run-store.md` and `svc-a/workspace.md`, while adding a boundary only if existing duplication warrants one.

An assumption-dropping option—showing only the workspace indicator or only producer revisions—is not viable under your recorded choices to retain all three surfaces and show eligible svc-a tags. Coordinated deployment is not used as a substitute for the revision-match contract.

I would switch from A to B only if implementation inspection reveals duplicated or inconsistent provenance assembly that a shared resolver would materially simplify.

Before kept it by stating both problems with the ask in two plain bullets right before the A/B/C question. To keep every fact Before kept while still delivering the Change (one option per physical line, lead-in first, Recommendation on its own last line — which After already does correctly), add a short premise paragraph to the first-message template that requires naming each flaw in the ask as framed before the options, e.g. "The ask as framed has two problems: a revision alone omits the visible processing date the outcome requires, and a workspace-wide revision on a file or item claims provenance that run may not have" — and make the premise-note strengthening say that concerns raised by the gather framing must be restated in the first message even when the fixtures already resolve them, rather than deferred to the approaches message. Everything else (pivot, surfaces, selection, missing, release) survived the new layout and expanded assembly intact.
